newsitem.title: USA: U.S. manufacturers' chief concerned by dollar rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. manufacturers' chief concerned by dollar rise.

text.p: The head of the National Association of Manufacturers voiced concern on Tuesday about the dollar's rise over the last few months and said a further appreciation would sharply slow U.S. economic growth.
"Exchange rate developments in the last few months are a cause for concern," association president Jerry Jasinowski said in a statement released at the start of a news conference.
"The current level of the dollar is preventing the expected boom in U.S. exports from occurring," he said.
"A further appreciation of the dollar would significantly slow the already moderate economic expansion," Jasinowski said.
"If the current expansion is to continue, everything possible must be done to increase exports by not letting our trading partners prop up the dollar for their own short-term gain," he added.
